_schema.purpose: Expected firing cadence + grace per Pulse check (I-XII), driving scripts/heal_pulse_check_staleness.py. The watcher alerts (pulse-check-stale:<id>) when a check's last success heartbeat is older than cadence_hours + grace_hours.
_schema.fail_closed: A check the watcher knows about (canonical set, or any pulse-check-<id>.heartbeat on disk) with NO entry here, or a malformed entry, gets a pulse-check-no-cadence:<id> alert rather than being silently unmonitored. Every rule earns enforcement.

fields.cadence_hours: Expected max gap between successful firings, in hours. Required unless event_driven.
fields.grace_hours: Slack added to cadence before alerting, to absorb a cycle that fires a few hours late. Defaults to 0 if absent.
fields.event_driven: true => the check fires on an external trigger (not a clock), so time-based staleness does not apply; the watcher skips it. It still emits heartbeats and failure envelopes.
fields.label: Human-readable check name (for the alert body).
fields.firing: Which scheduler fires the check (the systemd timer unit; exact wall-clock time lives ONLY in the unit file to avoid drift). Documentation only — the watcher reads cadence_hours/grace_hours.

_schema.tuning_note: As of 2026-07-07 every periodic check fires from its own systemd timer (ourliberty-pulse-check-<id>.timer) — agent-invoked /cycle scheduling is retired (the agent chronically missed late runbook sections; journal G-rules check-iii-invoke-gap-sunday-001 and check-ix-x-invoke-gap-monday-001). Grace absorbs a slow run or a Persistent catch-up after downtime; Check I is the tightest because it is the most frequent canary. These are conservative starting points and are Pulse-tunable (Check III self-tunes thresholds over time).

i.label: Optimization digest
i.firing: Mon/Wed/Fri/Sun, after Ledger's Monday run (systemd timer: ourliberty-pulse-check-i)

iii.label: Stuck-threshold review
iii.firing: Every Sunday (systemd timer: ourliberty-pulse-check-iii; the analyzer's artifact-anchored gate skips the off week of the 14-day cadence)
